title: Complete List of Indian Rivers and Their Tributaries

blocks.content: The Ganga river system is the largest river basin in India, sustaining millions of lives across northern and eastern plains.

rows: Form large meanders and extensive deltas
Shorter courses; East-flowing form deltas, West-flowing form estuaries

items: Memorize the Panch Prayag confluences on the Alaknanda River: Vishnuprayag (Dhauliganga), Nandaprayag (Nandakini), Karnaprayag (Pindar), Rudraprayag (Mandakini), and Devprayag (Bhagirathi).
Differentiate between East-flowing Peninsular rivers (Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Cauvery forming deltas) and West-flowing Peninsular rivers (Narmada, Tapti forming estuaries).
Identify Indus tributaries flowing through India: Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej, along with the Indus Waters Treaty allocation rules.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Ganga is the longest river in India, originating from the Gangotri Glacier as Bhagirathi and joining the Alaknanda at Devprayag.
Himalayan rivers are perennial and fed by both melting glaciers and rainfall, whereas Peninsular rivers are seasonal and primarily rain-fed.
The Godavari is the largest Peninsular river system and is commonly referred to as 'Dakshin Ganga' or 'Vridha Ganga'.
Major right-bank tributaries of the Ganga include the Yamuna and Son, while left-bank tributaries include the Ramganga, Gomti, Ghaghara, Gandak, and Kosi.
Narmada and Tapti flow westward through rift valleys between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges and drain into the Arabian Sea, forming estuaries instead of deltas.
